01 / FIELD NOTE

Look at the trees, then the ground.

Oak and beech woods are a useful Surrey starting point. Check shaded leaf litter, sheltered hollows, and fallen hardwood. Dead wood hosts different fungi from living tree roots; your habitat choice matters as much as the weather.

Explore Surrey Wildlife Trust’s fungi guide ↗
A scouting guide, not an identification or edibility check.

Photos show examples, not diagnostic proof. Similar species can be poisonous. Never eat a mushroom based on this app; seek in-person expert identification. Check landowner permission and site rules before collecting.

READING THE SIGNALS

Evidence, not certainty.

The app combines a broad UK habitat guide with additional species discovered in nearby seasonal records. Local candidates are not restricted to the guide. Some local candidates do not yet have documented ecology here, so they show a record-based label without a weather score. The default view includes seasonal guide species and all local candidates; choose the entire guide to include other seasons. It combines species ecology with recent model-based weather and community observations. It does not survey a wood, identify mushrooms, or predict an exact probability of finding one.

1. Recent weather

Open-Meteo supplies the last 14 completed local calendar days: daily precipitation and minimum/maximum air temperature. These are gridded model estimates, not guaranteed nearby rain-gauge readings. Yesterday’s minimum is a proxy for overnight conditions, not a measurement of soil temperature.

2. Historical local evidence

iNaturalist research-grade records within 30 km, in the current calendar month across all years, provide local and seasonal context. We retrieve paginated species-count results, up to 3,000 taxa, and keep species-level results. A cap is disclosed if reached. All returned species can appear, including those outside the habitat guide. Non-species groups are excluded. Taxonomic synonyms for several common fungi are reconciled. Observer effort and misidentification can bias the data. No record does not mean a species is absent; records can be outside Surrey at county borders.

3. Sorting and scouting signals

Species with local records appear first, sorted by their historical record count. This is an occurrence lead, not a likelihood estimate: conspicuous species and frequently visited sites can dominate. The habitat guide provides additional candidates, including ones with no returned records. Candidates without guide ecology have no weather or temperature score.

Guide species get 2 points for a broad UK season, 2 if the last 7 days had at least 10 mm of rain (1 for at least 3 mm), 1 if a day with at least 5 mm fell 2–7 days ago, 1 when the 3-day mean air temperature falls in an available broad scouting range (only some entries have one), and 1 for matching local records. At 5+ points we show “Worth a look”, at 3–4 “Possible”, otherwise “Fewer signals”. Off-season results are always “Season less typical”. Missing weather is never scored.

These thresholds and temperature ranges are exploratory rules chosen for this app, not published species-specific fruiting models. Wood-decay fungi may fruit at different intervals from soil fungi. Rainfall timing alone cannot establish which species is fruiting.

Sources & photography

The original detailed guide entries link to individual First Nature pages. Expanded guide entries have general UK habitat and season notes compiled for this app, with links to the fungi reference index and a scientific-name background search. These added notes have not been independently source-checked or expert-validated in this build. Local-only candidates link to the actual observation records; habitat is never inferred from a name or photograph. Local context comes from Surrey Wildlife Trust. Sightings and credited reference photos come from iNaturalist. Weather data by Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0).

Offline & privacy

The app keeps its shell, guide photos, and your last report on this device for offline use. Reports show their original fetch time; refresh online before heading out. Your chosen coordinates are sent to Open-Meteo and iNaturalist to obtain data. Town searches go to Open-Meteo. There is no app analytics or account. To remove local data, clear this site's browser storage.

Install on your phone

On Android, use your browser’s “Install app” or “Add to home screen”. On iPhone, open in Safari and choose Share → Add to Home Screen. Browser support and hosted sign-in can affect offline access; the app is packaged with a manifest and service worker.
